ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure below schematically shows the length of time that five different locations in a coastal area are affected by pressure belts and wind belts. <image1> Considering only the influence of atmospheric circulation, which location in the figure has relatively large seasonal variation in precipitation? ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled “subtropical high-pressure control time (months)”, and upward indicates the number of months under the control of the subtropical high pressure; the left side of the horizontal axis is labeled “trade wind control time (months)”, and the right side is labeled “westerly wind control time (months)”. The approximate positions of the five points are: ① about 10 months under subtropical high-pressure control and 2 months under trade wind control; ② about 12 months under subtropical high-pressure control; ③ about 8 months under subtropical high-pressure control and 4 months under westerly wind control; ④ about 4 months under subtropical high-pressure control and 8 months under westerly wind control; ⑤ about 11 months under westerly wind control and 1 month under subtropical high-pressure control. Then reason: when only considering the influence of atmospheric circulation, subtropical high-pressure control is mainly dominated by descending air currents, with little precipitation; coastal areas are more likely to obtain precipitation when under westerly wind control. The seasonal variation in precipitation should be relatively large where there is both an obvious dry season controlled by the subtropical high and a relatively long rainy season controlled by the westerlies. Point ④ has about a 4-month dry period and about an 8-month rainy period, with the most obvious transition and contrast between dry and wet seasons, so choose ④.
